from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "The Privacy Dilemma: Public Health vs. Personal Secret"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Traditional contact tracing often risks personal privacy.",
            "Centralized servers track your location and identity.",
            "DP-3T offers a privacy-first, decentralized alternative."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors
        VIRUS_COLOR = "#FF4500" # OrangeRed
        EYE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF" # White
        SHIELD_COLOR = "#00FF7F" # SpringGreen
        NODE_COLOR = WHITE
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color current lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(VIRUS_COLOR)
        
        # Create user network
        nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=NODE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=2) for _ in range(6)])
        node_grid_positions = ["B2", "B5", "C4", "D2", "E5", "F3"]
        for i, pos in enumerate(node_grid_positions):
            self.place_at_grid(nodes[i], pos)
            
        edges = VGroup(
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[1].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[3].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[4].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
            Line(nodes[3].get_center(), nodes[5].get_center(), color=GREY, stroke_width=2),
        )
        
        # Virus Mobject (represented as a spiked circle)
        virus_core = Circle(radius=0.15, color=VIRUS_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        spikes = VGroup(*[Line(ORIGIN, 0.25 * RIGHT, color=VIRUS_COLOR, stroke_width=3).rotate(a) for a in np.linspace(0, 2*PI, 8)])
        virus = VGroup(virus_core, spikes)
        self.place_at_grid(virus, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(nodes), Create(edges), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(virus))
        
        # Virus spreading sequence
        self.play(nodes[0].animate.set_color(VIRUS_COLOR))
        self.play(virus.animate.move_to(self.grid["C4"]), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(nodes[2].animate.set_color(VIRUS_COLOR))
        self.play(virus.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"]), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(nodes[3].animate.set_color(VIRUS_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update lecture line colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(EYE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Create 'Eye' icon
        # Using specific vectors for ArcBetweenPoints to ensure stability
        start_pt = np.array([-0.5, 0, 0])
        end_pt = np.array([0.5, 0, 0])
        eye_top = ArcBetweenPoints(start_pt, end_pt, angle=-PI/2, color=EYE_COLOR)
        eye_bottom = ArcBetweenPoints(start_pt, end_pt, angle=PI/2, color=EYE_COLOR)
        iris = Circle(radius=0.15, color=EYE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5)
        pupil = Dot(radius=0.07, color=EYE_COLOR)
        eye = VGroup(eye_top, eye_bottom, iris, pupil)
        self.place_in_area(eye, "A3", "A4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Surveillance lines (data collection)
        data_lines = VGroup(*[
            Line(node.get_center(), eye.get_center(), color=EYE_COLOR, stroke_width=1).set_opacity(0.4)
            for node in nodes
        ])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(eye))
        self.play(Create(data_lines), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update lecture line colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(SHIELD_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Shield icon
        shield_shape = Polygon(
            [-0.4, 0.4, 0], [0.4, 0.4, 0], [0.4, -0.2, 0], [0, -0.5, 0], [-0.4, -0.2, 0],
            color=SHIELD_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8
        )
        shield = VGroup(shield_shape)
        self.place_in_area(shield, "A3", "A4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Transition: Shield replaces Eye and data lines vanish
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(eye, shield),
            data_lines.animate.set_opacity(0),
        )
        
        # Protection effect (nodes glow or get a green circle)
        protections = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.18, color=SHIELD_COLOR, stroke_width=3).move_to(node.get_center())
            for node in nodes
        ])
        
        self.play(Create(protections), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite 1: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) & Hashing"
        lines = [
            "Bluetooth Low Energy enables short-range digital handshakes.",
            "Cryptographic hashing turns secret keys into random IDs.",
            "These one-way functions prevent reversing the random IDs."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        BLE_BLUE = "#1E90FF"
        KEY_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        HASH_GRAY = "#A9A9A9"
        ID_LIME = "#ADFF2F"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLE_BLUE))
        
        # Phone Icons
        phone1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.2, width=0.7, color=WHITE)
        phone2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.2, width=0.7, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(phone1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(phone2, "B5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(phone1), FadeIn(phone2))
        
        # Concentric Rings
        def get_rings(center):
            rings = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2 * i, color=BLE_BLUE, stroke_opacity=1 - 0.2*i) for i in range(1, 5)])
            rings.move_to(center)
            return rings

        rings1 = get_rings(self.grid["B2"])
        rings2 = get_rings(self.grid["B5"])
        
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(*[r.animate.scale(1.5).set_stroke(opacity=0) for r in rings1], lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=2),
            LaggedStart(*[r.animate.scale(1.5).set_stroke(opacity=0) for r in rings2], lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=2),
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(KEY_GOLD),
            FadeOut(phone1), FadeOut(phone2)
        )
        
        # Secret Key
        secret_key = Text("Secret Key", font_size=20, color=KEY_GOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(secret_key, "E1")
        
        # Hash Box
        hash_box = Square(side_length=1.2, color=HASH_GRAY, fill_opacity=0.5)
        hash_label = Text("Hash\nFunction", font_size=16, color=WHITE).move_to(hash_box.get_center())
        hash_group = VGroup(hash_box, hash_label)
        self.place_in_area(hash_group, "E3", "E4")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(secret_key), FadeIn(hash_group))
        
        # Unique ID (initially hidden)
        unique_id = Text("8a3f...2e", font_size=20, color=ID_LIME)
        self.place_at_grid(unique_id, "E6")

        # Move key into box
        self.play(secret_key.animate.move_to(hash_group.get_center()).scale(0.5).set_opacity(0), run_time=1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(ID_LIME)
        )
        
        # Unique ID exits
        self.play(FadeIn(unique_id, shift=RIGHT), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Attempt to reverse (visualize failure)
        cross = Cross(unique_id, color=RED).scale(1.2)
        arrow_back = Arrow(start=self.grid["E6"], end=self.grid["E4"], color=RED)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow_back))
        self.play(Create(cross))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "The Daily Cycle: Generating Ephemeral IDs (EphID)"
        lines = [
            "Every day, your phone generates a Secret Day Key.",
            "From this key, it derives multiple Ephemeral IDs.",
            "These random IDs change every fifteen minutes.",
            "Frequent rotation prevents anyone from tracking your device.",
            "Your true identity remains hidden behind these IDs."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        GOLD = "#FFD700"
        SKY_BLUE = "#87CEEB"
        WHITE_CLR = "#FFFFFF"
        RED_CLR = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Every day, your phone generates a Secret Day Key.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        
        sk_t_node = Circle(radius=0.5, color=GOLD, fill_opacity=0.3)
        sk_t_label = Text("SK_t", color=GOLD, font_size=24)
        sk_t_group = VGroup(sk_t_node, sk_t_label)
        self.place_in_area(sk_t_group, "A2", "B3")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sk_t_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # From this key, it derives multiple Ephemeral IDs.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(SKY_BLUE))
        
        eph_ids = VGroup()
        positions = ["D1", "D2", "D3", "D4"]
        arrows = VGroup()
        
        for i, pos in enumerate(positions):
            eph_node = RoundedRectangle(height=0.6, width=1.2, corner_radius=0.1, color=SKY_BLUE, fill_opacity=0.2)
            eph_label = Text(f"EphID_{i+1}", color=SKY_BLUE, font_size=18)
            eph_group = VGroup(eph_node, eph_label)
            self.place_at_grid(eph_group, pos)
            eph_ids.add(eph_group)
            
            arrow = Arrow(sk_t_group.get_bottom(), eph_group.get_top(), buff=0.1, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
            arrows.add(arrow)

        self.play(LaggedStart(*(GrowArrow(arr) for arr in arrows), lag_ratio=0.3))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*(FadeIn(eid) for eid in eph_ids), lag_ratio=0.3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # These random IDs change every fifteen minutes.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE_CLR))
        
        time_labels = ["00:00", "00:15", "00:30", "00:45"]
        v_time_texts = VGroup()
        for i, tid in enumerate(time_labels):
            t_text = Text(tid, font_size=14, color=GRAY).next_to(eph_ids[i], DOWN, buff=0.1)
            v_time_texts.add(t_text)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(v_time_texts))
        self.play(Indicate(eph_ids[0]), run_time=1)
        self.play(Indicate(eph_ids[1]), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 & 5 ===
        # Privacy and protection
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(RED_CLR), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(RED_CLR))
        
        # Cross out a "Tracker" symbol
        tracker_text = Text("TRACKER", color=RED_CLR, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(tracker_text, "F2")
        cross = Cross(tracker_text)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(tracker_text))
        self.play(Create(cross))
        
        # Final identity mask
        phone = Icon(name="mobile-alt", color=WHITE).scale(0.5) if "Icon" in globals() else Square(side_length=0.6, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(phone, "A5")
        secret_label = Text("True ID", color=WHITE, font_size=18).next_to(phone, UP)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(phone), FadeIn(secret_label))
        shield = SurroundingRectangle(phone, color=GOLD, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(shield))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "The Encounter: Recording the Digital Handshake"
        lecture_lines = [
            "When phones meet, they exchange rotating Ephemeral IDs.",
            "Your phone records the signal strength and ID.",
            "This data is stored locally on your device only.",
            "No location or personal information is ever exchanged.",
            "The central server knows nothing about this meeting."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        alice_color = "#00BFFF"
        bob_color = "#FF69B4"
        diary_color = "#F5DEB3"
        ghost_color = "#A9A9A9"
        server_color = "#808080"
        red_color = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # When phones meet, they exchange rotating Ephemeral IDs.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(alice_color)
        
        alice_icon = Circle(radius=0.4, color=alice_color, fill_opacity=0.3)
        alice_label = Text("Alice", font_size=18, color=alice_color).next_to(alice_icon, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        alice = VGroup(alice_icon, alice_label)
        
        bob_icon = Circle(radius=0.4, color=bob_color, fill_opacity=0.3)
        bob_label = Text("Bob", font_size=18, color=bob_color).next_to(bob_icon, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        bob = VGroup(bob_icon, bob_label)
        
        self.place_at_grid(alice, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(bob, 'B5')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(alice), FadeIn(bob))
        self.play(
            alice.animate.move_to(self.grid['B3']),
            bob.animate.move_to(self.grid['B4'])
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Your phone records the signal strength and ID.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(bob_color)
        
        id_a = Text("ID_A1", font_size=14, color=WHITE)
        id_b = Text("ID_B1", font_size=14, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(id_a, 'B3')
        self.place_at_grid(id_b, 'B4')
        
        self.play(
            id_a.animate.move_to(self.grid['B4']),
            id_b.animate.move_to(self.grid['B3']),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        signal_strength = Text("RSSI: -65dBm", font_size=12, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(signal_strength, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(signal_strength))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # This data is stored locally on your device only.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(diary_color)
        
        diary_a = Square(side_length=0.6, color=diary_color, fill_opacity=0.5)
        label_diary_a = Text("Local Diary", font_size=12, color=diary_color).next_to(diary_a, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        diary_group_a = VGroup(diary_a, label_diary_a)
        
        diary_b = Square(side_length=0.6, color=diary_color, fill_opacity=0.5)
        label_diary_b = Text("Local Diary", font_size=12, color=diary_color).next_to(diary_b, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        diary_group_b = VGroup(diary_b, label_diary_b)
        
        self.place_at_grid(diary_group_a, 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(diary_group_b, 'D4')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(diary_group_a), FadeIn(diary_group_b))
        
        # Move IDs into diaries
        self.play(
            id_b.animate.move_to(diary_a.get_center()).scale(0.5),
            id_a.animate.move_to(diary_b.get_center()).scale(0.5),
            signal_strength.animate.move_to(diary_a.get_center()).scale(0.5).set_opacity(0)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # No location or personal information is ever exchanged.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(ghost_color)
        
        gps_base = Circle(radius=0.15, color=ghost_color)
        gps_point = Triangle(color=ghost_color).scale(0.15).rotate(180*DEGREES).next_to(gps_base, DOWN, buff=0)
        gps_icon = VGroup(gps_base, gps_point)
        
        id_head = Circle(radius=0.1, color=ghost_color)
        id_body = Rectangle(width=0.3, height=0.2, color=ghost_color).next_to(id_head, DOWN, buff=0.05)

outline.topic: DP-3T: The Privacy-Preserving Shield for Contact Tracing
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Cybersecurity) and tech-savvy professionals

sections.title: The Privacy Dilemma: Public Health vs. Personal Secret
sections.content: Introduce the challenge of tracking virus spread without creating a 'Big Brother' surveillance state. Contrast 'Centralized' (government knows all) vs. 'Decentralized' (DP-3T) approaches. Establish the core goal: notifying people of exposure without anyone—even the server—knowing who met whom.
sections.example: Alice and Bob meet in a park. Alice wants to know if Bob gets sick later, but she doesn't want a central server to track their GPS locations or identities.

sections.title: Prerequisite 1: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) & Hashing
sections.content: Explain the two technical pillars: 1. BLE Beacons (short-range 'digital handshakes' that don't use GPS). 2. Cryptographic Hash Functions (one-way functions that turn a secret key into a random-looking ID).
sections.example: Visual: A 'Secret Key' (a gold coin) goes through a 'Meat Grinder' (Hash Function) to produce a 'Unique Tag' (a numbered ticket). You can't turn the ticket back into the coin.

sections.title: The Daily Cycle: Generating Ephemeral IDs (EphID)
sections.content: Explain the generation of rotating IDs. Each phone generates a 'Secret Day Key' ($SK_t$). From this, it derives multiple 'Ephemeral IDs' (EphIDs) that change every 15 minutes to prevent tracking.
sections.example: Graph: A timeline showing Alice's phone broadcasting 'ID_A1' at 10:00 AM, then switching to 'ID_A2' at 10:15 AM. To a bystander, these look like two completely different devices.

sections.title: The Encounter: Recording the Digital Handshake
sections.content: When Alice and Bob are close, their phones exchange and locally store the received EphIDs and the signal strength (to estimate distance). Crucially, this data stays ONLY on the phones.
sections.example: Animation: Alice's 'digital diary' records Bob's random ID '8F3D...' and the date. Bob's diary records Alice's random ID '2A9B...'. Neither knows the other's name.

sections.title: The Infection Report: Uploading the Secret Key
sections.content: If Bob tests positive, he voluntarily uploads his *Secret Day Keys* ($SK_t$) for the past 14 days to a central server. He does NOT upload his contact list or his location.
sections.example: Bob's phone sends a small list of 14 'Secret Keys' to a public bulletin board. The board now says: 'Someone who had these keys is sick,' but it doesn't say who.

sections.title: The Local Match: Privacy-First Verification
sections.content: Every day, Alice's phone downloads the new 'Secret Keys' from the server. It uses those keys to reconstruct all possible EphIDs that the sick person *would* have broadcast. It then checks for a match in its local diary.
sections.example: Mathematical Visualization: Local_Diary ∩ Generated_IDs_from_Keys = {Match?}. Alice's phone finds '8F3D...' in its diary and triggers a notification. The server is never involved in this check.

sections.title: Summary: Why DP-3T Wins
sections.content: Review the decentralized nature: 1. No identity disclosure. 2. No location tracking. 3. The server is just a 'dumb' mailbox for keys. The intelligence and privacy remain at the 'edge' (on the users' devices).
sections.example: Final Visual: A shield icon composed of rotating IDs protecting a group of character avatars (Alice, Bob, etc.) from a central watchful eye.

storyboard.title: The Privacy Dilemma: Public Health vs. Personal Secret
lecture_lines: Traditional contact tracing often risks personal privacy.
Centralized servers track your location and identity.
DP-3T offers a privacy-first, decentralized alternative.
animations: Virus icon (#FF4500) spreads through a network of white circles.
Large 'Eye' icon (#FFFFFF) appears above the network, collecting data.
Transition to a 'Shield' icon (#00FF7F) protecting the user nodes.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite 1: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) & Hashing
lecture_lines: Bluetooth Low Energy enables short-range digital handshakes.
Cryptographic hashing turns secret keys into random IDs.
These one-way functions prevent reversing the random IDs.
animations: Two phone icons emit blue concentric rings (#1E90FF) for BLE.
A 'Secret Key' text (#FFD700) enters a 'Hash Box' (#A9A9A9).
A 'Unique ID' string (#ADFF2F) exits the 'Hash Box'.

storyboard.title: The Daily Cycle: Generating Ephemeral IDs (EphID)
lecture_lines: Every day, your phone generates a Secret Day Key.
From this key, it derives multiple Ephemeral IDs.
These random IDs change every fifteen minutes.
Frequent rotation prevents anyone from tracking your device.
Your true identity remains hidden behind these IDs.
animations: Show 'Secret Day Key' ($SK_t$) as a gold node (#FFD700).
Generate multiple 'EphID' nodes (#87CEEB) branching from the key.
A clock icon (#FFFFFF) ticks, indicating time passing.
Highlight one EphID; previous one fades out each tick.
'Attacker' icon (#FF0000) tries and fails to link EphIDs.

storyboard.title: The Encounter: Recording the Digital Handshake
lecture_lines: When phones meet, they exchange rotating Ephemeral IDs.
Your phone records the signal strength and ID.
This data is stored locally on your device only.
No location or personal information is ever exchanged.
The central server knows nothing about this meeting.
animations: Alice and Bob icons (#00BFFF, #FF69B4) move close together.
Packet 'ID_A1' moves to Bob; 'ID_B1' moves to Alice.
'Local Diary' icon (#F5DEB3) appears on both phones [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg], storing IDs.
Ghostly 'GPS' and 'Identity' icons (#A9A9A9) appear with red strike-throughs.
A 'Server' icon (#808080) at the screen edge appears grayed out and disconnected.

storyboard.title: The Infection Report: Uploading the Secret Key
lecture_lines: If infected, users voluntarily upload their Secret Day Keys.
Only the keys are sent to the central server.
The server never receives contact lists or locations.
animations: Bob icon turns red (#FF0000) and selects 14 'Secret Day Keys' (#FFD700).
Keys (#FFD700) move to 'Cloud Server' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cloud.svg] (#F0F8FF) and then to a 'Public Bulletin Board' (#F5F5DC).
Red 'X' marks over 'Contacts' and 'GPS' icons (#A9A9A9) to show exclusion.

storyboard.title: The Local Match: Privacy-First Verification
lecture_lines: Phones download new Secret Day Keys from the server.
Your device reconstructs the infected person's rotating IDs.
It checks these IDs against its own local diary.
A match triggers a notification on your device.
The matching process happens entirely on your phone.
animations: Alice icon downloads 'Secret Keys' (#FFD700) from the server [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/server.svg].
Alice's phone icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] processes keys through a hash function box.
A list of 'Reconstructed IDs' (#87CEEB) fills the screen.
Compare 'Reconstructed IDs' with Alice's 'Local Diary' (#F5DEB3).
A match highlights in yellow (#FFFF00) and triggers 'Risk Alert'.

storyboard.title: Summary: Why DP-3T Wins
lecture_lines: DP-3T protects identity through decentralized key rotation.
Privacy is maintained by processing matches locally.
Public health and personal secrets can coexist safely.
animations: Central Server icon becomes a simple 'Mailbox' (#B22222).
User icons remain anonymous behind green shields (#00FF7F).
Text 'DP-3T: Public Health + Privacy' appears in white (#FFFFFF).
